# Proverbs 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Wisdom has-built her-house; she-has-hewn her-pillars seven.

**2** She-has-slaughtered her-slaughter; she-has-mixed her-wine; also she-has-set her-table.

**3** She-has-sent-out her-maidens; she-calls upon [the]-heights-of [the]-summits-of [the]-city:

**4** "Whoever [is]-simple, let-him-turn-in here." [To the one]-lacking heart she-says to-him,

**5** "Come, eat of-my-bread, and-drink of-[the]-wine I-have-mixed.

**6** Forsake simple-ones and-live, and-walk in-[the]-way-of understanding."

**7** One-correcting a-scoffer takes for-himself shame, and-one-rebuking a-wicked-one — his-blemish.

**8** Do-not-rebuke a-scoffer lest he-hate-you; rebuke a-wise-man and-he-will-love-you.

**9** Give to-a-wise-man and-he-will-be-yet-wiser; inform a-righteous-man and-he-will-increase learning.

**10** Beginning-of wisdom [is]-fear-of YHWH, and-knowledge-of [the]-Holy-One [is]-understanding.

**11** For by-me your-days will-be-multiplied, and-years-of life will-be-added to-you.

**12** If you-are-wise, you-are-wise for-yourself; and-if you-scoff, alone you-will-bear-[it].

**13** Woman-of foolishness [is]-boisterous, simplicity — and-she-does-not-know anything.

**14** And-she-sits at-[the]-door-of her-house, upon a-seat [on the]-heights-of [the]-city,

**15** To-call to-those-passing-by [on the]-way, those-making-straight their-paths:

**16** "Whoever [is]-simple, let-him-turn-in here." And-[to the one]-lacking heart she-says to-him,

**17** "Waters-of stealth are-sweet, and-bread-of secrecy is-pleasant."

**18** And-he-does-not-know that [the]-shades [are]-there; in-[the]-depths-of Sheol [are] her-invited-ones.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **9:1**: Shiv'ah ammudeha — 'her seven pillars.' The number seven suggests completeness. The identity of the 'seven pillars' has generated extensive speculation.

- **9:10**: Qedoshim (Holy One) — plural of majesty. Returns to the thesis of 1:7 but deepens it: knowledge of God Himself, not just fear/reverence.

- **9:17**: Mayim-genuvim — 'stolen waters.' Folly's offer is the mirror-image of Wisdom's feast: both invite the simple, but Folly's appeal is to the thrill of the forbidden.

— EMET
